packs.name: Basics
packs.note: The plain set: round, soft, ink, pencil, charcoal, marker, chisel, bristle, two wet brushes that pick up the colour under them, a marker whose edge wicks into the paper, and a brush whose grain streaks along the stroke.

packs.name: Glyph stamps
packs.note: His glyphs as stamps, from the Design Kit.

brushes.name: Glyph Guy
brushes.note: His glyph from the Design Kit (glyphs/glyph-guy.png) as a stamp: tap to place it, Size sets its largest side, it paints in the current colour.

brushes.name: Love Yourself
brushes.note: His glyph from the Design Kit (glyphs/love-yourself.png) as a stamp: tap to place it, Size sets its largest side, it paints in the current colour.

brushes.name: Money glyph
brushes.note: His glyph from the Design Kit (glyphs/money.png) as a stamp: tap to place it, Size sets its largest side, it paints in the current colour.

brushes.name: Poverty to luxury
brushes.note: His glyph from the Design Kit (glyphs/poverty-to-luxury.png) as a stamp: tap to place it, Size sets its largest side, it paints in the current colour.

brushes.name: Smiley
brushes.note: His glyph from the Design Kit (glyphs/smiley.png) as a stamp: tap to place it, Size sets its largest side, it paints in the current colour.

packs.name: His bands
packs.note: Bands with a filled middle and a line down each edge (his olive and teal, pink and purple, red and black cards). No clearance: the band drawn on top stays whole and the one under stops at its edge line.

brushes.name: Bone band
brushes.note: Two bold black lines with the middle filled bone: his picture of two black bands with a white middle. The size is the whole band.

brushes.name: Green band
brushes.note: A sage-green band with a thin teal line down each edge, as in his olive and teal watercolour bands. The one drawn on top stays whole; the one under stops at its edge line.

brushes.name: Pink band
brushes.note: A salmon-pink band edged with a thin purple line each side, as on his pink-on-purple card.

brushes.name: Gold band
brushes.note: A gold band with a thin obsidian line down each edge.

brushes.name: Red band
brushes.note: A red band with black edge lines, as on his red and black crayon card.

brushes.name: Tube band
brushes.note: Glossy tube edges with a deep blue middle: the tube pair of his references, as one band.

packs.name: His hand
packs.note: Brushes that behave like his art and the curve hero. Every one clears a channel around itself, as the curve hero does. Each names the reference image(s) in refs/ it was made from, and carries its own Design Kit colour so it can be told apart.

brushes.name: Oil pastel
brushes.note: His oil-pastel stroke: thick wax, rough bled edge, paper tooth that is irregular (a woven grain read as a checkerboard and was wrong).

brushes.name: Pastel wash
brushes.note: The same wax laid light, so the paper shows through; streaky.

brushes.name: Ledger pen
brushes.note: His ledger-page pen: thin, even, a little shake, no point.

brushes.name: Curve hero
brushes.note: The curve hero as a brush: a flat-ended band that cuts its own clearance out of everything beneath it (pl-headless GoldCurves CHANNEL = 9, butt caps).

brushes.name: Curve pair
brushes.note: The curve hero band with its companion band beside it and the channel clearing both.

brushes.name: Tube
brushes.note: Glossy tube: light top edge, the colour, a dark core, a hue-shifted rim; flat ends; the light stays on one side whichever way the stroke travels. Drawn as a double, two parallel tubes, as in the references.

brushes.name: Crayon pair
brushes.note: A thick wax band with a thinner companion line beside it in the second colour, touching or slightly overlapping, flat ends (his three paper studies: red with black, green with blue, orange with blue).

brushes.name: Wax relief
brushes.note: Heavy lumpy relief grain with the companion bleeding underneath; the wax stands up off the paper. A double: two parallel lines, each with its companion.

brushes.name: Pastel bleed
brushes.note: Orange body with the second colour bleeding soft and grainy beneath it. A double, as in the reference.

brushes.name: Curve swell
brushes.note: A single curve stroke: swells and thins with pressure, flat ends, never a pointed tip (curve rules S310).

brushes.name: Flat paint
brushes.note: Flat acrylic bands on black: a thick single band, hard edge with a little dry-brush rag, flat cut ends, almost no change of width (his yellow study).

brushes.name: Keyline hero
brushes.note: The curve hero with its channel filled in a contrasting colour: the keyline and the clearance are one object (his Machine Spec R29, the keyline-weave register).

brushes.name: Glow curve
brushes.note: The channel glows (R11, the emissive register; his glow-in-the-dark painting). Best on a black ground.

brushes.name: Stacked hero
brushes.note: Two channels stacked, light then dark (R33), heavier on the outer side (R66 asymmetric keyline).

brushes.name: Tooth pastel
brushes.note: Oil pastel whose wax fills the paper's grain where you press hard (Tooth), and whose grain sits elsewhere on every stroke so a second pass fills what the first left (Burnish).

brushes.name: Resolve ribbon
brushes.note: The curve hero whose end folds closed into a diamond instead of a flat cut (his R49 terminals: stop or resolve).

brushes.name: Support hero
brushes.note: An end with no room to taper gets wider, not thinner: the support base (his R5).

brushes.name: Satellite pastel
brushes.note: Oil pastel that drops a few small marks near its contour (his R75, the IMG_1190 plate).

brushes.name: Weave hero
brushes.note: Interlace: the first crossing goes over, the next under, the next over (his R44; the archive has about 290 interlaced and interlocking pieces). Clears at the sides so the gaps stay clean.

brushes.name: Echo pen
brushes.note: A band that draws its own inner echoes when you lift: concentric clear lines collapsing to the centre (his R21 and R25).

presets: ATC card 2.5 x 3.5 in at 300 dpi
Small card 4 x 6 in at 300 dpi
Square card 5 x 5 in at 300 dpi
Sketchbook page 8.5 x 11 in at 200 dpi
canvases._about: New canvas presets. The card sizes come from his physical work (ATC and small cards, 64 cards in the archive); the tile and the strip are for his tiling registers (R45, directional strip).

quickmenu._about: The QuickMenu profiles PL Paint starts with: six buttons each, named from the action list in PL Paint (src/app.js QM_ACTIONS).

gestures._about: What each touch or pen gesture does when PL Paint starts. The names are PL Paint's action names (the QuickMenu list, src/app.js QM_ACTIONS) or None. Every one can be changed in Gesture controls.

study._about: The guided study session in PL Paint (Actions, Study). Each exercise is something Claude needs to see his hand do, so that Third Eye can draw the way he draws. `target` is how many strokes count as done (he can move on any time). `learn` says what the exercise teaches, so he knows why it is asked. Nothing is sent anywhere: the files stay in Documents, in the PL Paint folder.

exercises.name: Curves, end to end
exercises.prompt: Draw 8 long curves from one edge of the canvas to the other, the way you naturally do. Any direction. Don't think about it.
exercises.learn: your natural stroke: speed along the curve, the swell of pressure, where it wobbles

exercises.name: Slow, then fast
exercises.prompt: Draw the same curve 3 times as slowly as you can, then 3 times as fast as you can.
exercises.learn: how your line changes with speed (shake, width, overshoot)

exercises.name: Crossings
exercises.prompt: Draw 6 curves that cross each other, the way you do in your interlaced pieces. Go over or under as you would.
exercises.learn: how you handle a crossing: the gap, the order, which stroke you lift first

exercises.name: Starts and ends
exercises.prompt: Draw 10 short strokes. Think only about how you put the pen down and how you lift it.
exercises.learn: your starts and ends: pressure ramp, flat or soft, the little hook

exercises.name: Light to heavy
exercises.prompt: Draw 5 lines pressing from light to heavy, then 5 from heavy to light.
exercises.learn: your pressure range and how you move through it

exercises.name: As steady as you can
exercises.prompt: Draw 5 slow straight lines as steady as you can. Don't correct them.
exercises.learn: your tremor: its size and its rhythm

exercises.name: Doubles
exercises.prompt: Draw 6 doubles: a thick line with a thinner one beside it, as in your oil-pastel studies.
exercises.learn: how you draw a pair: which first, how close, the order

exercises.name: Filling a shape
exercises.prompt: Draw 3 shapes and fill them in the way you normally colour in.
exercises.learn: your fill strokes: direction, overlap, how you reach an edge

exercises.name: Your mark
exercises.prompt: Write or draw your signature or personal mark 10 times.
exercises.learn: your signature as drawn: for the lit-cell stamp, and the hand model's most personal data

exercises.name: Your glyphs
exercises.prompt: Draw your glyphs twice each: the heart, the smiley, the money glyph, Glyph Guy, Love Yourself.
exercises.learn: how you construct your own symbols: stroke order and direction

exercises.name: Fixing a mistake
exercises.prompt: Draw something, make a mistake on purpose, and fix it the way you usually do (undo, erase, draw over).
exercises.learn: your corrections: undo, erase or overdraw, and how fast

exercises.name: A free page
exercises.prompt: Draw whatever you would on a normal day. 20 minutes or more is ideal.
exercises.learn: everything else: your order of work, your pauses, your zoom and rotate habits

papers._about: Paper stocks for new canvases (PL Paint, New canvas and Actions). ground must be a Design Kit colour. texture: how the paper looks under the marks. edge: deckle gives the torn, handmade edge of his physical papers (the oil-pastel studies are on deckled paper).

names._about: Name It: qualities he pairs with his piece names (Source/VISUAL LEXICON.md: ELEGANCE, MYSTERY, RESILIENCE, ARTISTRY, with DEFIANCE-adjacent words throughout). The full bank of several hundred names is in his journal export, not in the vault: if he puts a file named names-bank.txt (one name per line, optionally `Name - QUALITY`) in the PL Paint folder, PL Paint uses that first.

shape._about: 'tip' is a brush tip imported from a Photoshop .abr file; the picture travels with the brush (PL Paint stores it in the brush's tip field).

color._about: The brush's own identity colour, from the Design Kit's colours, so the brushes can be told apart in a list or on a sheet. Optional.

color2._about: The companion colour for paired brushes, also from the Design Kit.

lines._about: Parallel lines in one stroke (his references are doubles).

lineGap._about: Space between the lines, as a share of brush size.

channelEnds._about: Where the clearance is cut: 'sides' only, as the curve hero does (butt caps), or 'all' round the stroke, ends too.

twinMode._about: 'over' draws the companion on top of the main band with a multiply blend, as his blue crosses his orange (dark olive where they meet).

wet._about: Wet mix: how much of the canvas colour under the brush the paint picks up. 0 is dry paint.

wetPull._about: Wet mix: how long the picked-up paint is carried before the brush's own colour returns. 1 never lets go, 0 returns almost at once.

channelColor._about: The colour a channel is filled with when its fill is colour or glow; a Design Kit colour. Unset: the second colour.

channel2Color._about: The colour a channel is filled with when its fill is colour or glow; a Design Kit colour. Unset: the second colour.

channelFill._about: R29: the keyline and the clearance are one object, only the fill differs: ground (clear), a contrasting colour, glow, or a soft shadow.

channel2Fill._about: The fill of the second, outer channel (R33: channels stack, light then dark).

channelAsym._about: R66: -1 to 1, how much heavier the channel is on one side of the travel than the other.

channel2._about: Size of a second channel outside the first, as a share of brush size.

tremor._about: R73: the hand's shake as a share of the brush width; each rail shakes on its own, so the band's width wobbles too. His spec: 0.06.

swell._about: R7: slow width modulation along the stroke without any pressure (0.2 to 0.45 in his spec).

swellLen._about: How long one swell is, in brush widths.

flareStart._about: R5: the start widens instead of thinning (the support base).

flareEnd._about: R5: the end widens instead of thinning.

capStart._about: R49: how the start ends: stop (flat cut) or resolve (fold closed).

capEnd._about: R49: how the end ends: stop (flat cut) or resolve (fold closed).

grainDrift._about: Burnish: each stroke lays its grain at a different place, so a second pass fills what the first left.

pressGrain._about: Tooth: pressing harder fills the paper's grain with wax.

grainStretch._about: For grain 'along': how far the grain is pulled out along the stroke.

wick._about: Marker: after the stroke the edge spreads into the paper, more where it is rough.

satellites._about: R75: small marks dropped near the stroke's contour.

echo._about: Echo Pen: how many inner echoes the stroke draws inside its own band when you lift (R21 inner echo, R25 stacked echoes read as folds).

echoStep._about: Echo Pen: the space between echoes, as a share of brush size.

echoGap._about: Echo Pen: how thick the clear line of each echo is, as a share of brush size.

weave._about: R44 interlace: over 0, a stroke that crosses an earlier one goes over at the first crossing, under at the next, over at the next.

tiltSize._about: Pen tilt widens the mark, the way the side of a pencil does.

tiltAngle._about: The mark turns to follow which way the pen leans.

hueJit._about: Colour dynamics: each dab's hue varies a little (up to 60 degrees at 1).

satJit._about: Colour dynamics: each dab's saturation varies.

briJit._about: Colour dynamics: each dab's lightness varies.

gapFill._about: Between the parallel lines of a stroke: 'colour' lays a solid band in the middle (his doubles with the middle filled), so what is under it is hidden and the two lines cross other strokes as one band.

gapFillColor._about: The colour of the filled middle; a Design Kit colour. Unset: the companion colour.

edge._about: Band mode, with lines = 2 and gapFill = colour: the brush size is the whole band, and each edge line takes this share of it (his bands are a filled middle with a thin line down each edge, olive with teal, pink with purple). 0 = the lines are as wide as the brush, as in a plain double.

join._about: Band mode: a stroke that starts inside an earlier band of the same fill grows out of it. Where its edge lines would run across that band they are left out, and its fill covers the band's edge line there, so the two read as one shape with the lines flowing round (his stems branching off a trunk). 0 = off.

joinMode._about: Band mode with join on: 'auto' (default) reads how the stroke meets the earlier band: steeply it is a T (the earlier outline stays whole, R87), along it the outlines flow together (R27); 'tee' and 'flow' force one.

edgeRound._about: Band mode: how much the band's heading eases into a turn. 0 = the edge lines fold at a point; higher = they sweep round the corner as a soft fillet (his bands, refs 13, 14, 19: one continuous pen line).

edgeSwell._about: Band mode: how much the edge line thickens where the band turns, so the line swells at corners as a pen line does.

colourSense._about: Colour Sense: what his own writing says each colour means. Source: Source/VISUAL LEXICON.md (the colour signature table and his sign vocabulary from the journal). A colour whose meaning he has not written is named by family only, and says so. h in degrees, s and l 0 to 1.

families.name: Black
families.meaning: The void, absence, the condition before emergence.

families.name: Gold
families.meaning: Declaration. Gold on black is the brand's signature axis.

families.name: Oxblood
families.meaning: The energy of the personality: sacrifice and survival.

families.name: Blue
families.meaning: The Totem's base, the landed ground.

families.name: Warm red or orange
families.meaning: The warm family, with gold and oxblood, is the register the brand declares as home.

families.name: White or bone
families.meaning: The starkest statement of void and bone, in black and white.
